reference.source: Nelson Textbook of Pediatrics / standard metabolic references
clinicalPearls: An autosomal recessive leukodystrophy caused by deficiency of the enzyme arylsulfatase A, leading to accumulation of sulfatides and progressive demyelination of central and peripheral nervous systems
The late-infantile form is most common, presenting in the second year with gait disturbance, weakness, and loss of previously acquired motor skills
Peripheral neuropathy with depressed or absent deep tendon reflexes is characteristic and can accompany central signs
Juvenile and adult forms present later, often with behavioural change, cognitive decline, or psychiatric symptoms before motor deterioration
MRI shows symmetrical confluent white matter signal change, sometimes with a tigroid or leopard-skin pattern of spared perivascular regions
Elevated cerebrospinal fluid protein and slowed nerve conduction reflect the demyelinating process
A rare subset is due to deficiency of the sphingolipid activator protein saposin B rather than the enzyme itself
Haematopoietic stem cell transplantation and, in selected presymptomatic patients, gene therapy may modify the course, while established neurological damage is not reversed
reference.pathophysiology: Metachromatic leukodystrophy results from biallelic pathogenic variants in ARSA, encoding the lysosomal enzyme arylsulfatase A, which desulfates sulfatide (cerebroside sulfate). Deficient activity causes sulfatides to accumulate within lysosomes of myelin-forming cells (oligodendrocytes and Schwann cells) and other tissues. The accumulated sulfatide is toxic to myelin-producing cells, driving progressive demyelination of the central and peripheral nervous system and the resulting motor, cognitive, and neuropathic decline. Stored material stains metachromatically, giving the disease its name.
additionalDifferentials: Other leukodystrophies such as X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy
additionalInvestigations: Assay of arylsulfatase A enzyme activity, interpreted with awareness of pseudodeficiency alleles
ARSA molecular genetic testing to confirm the diagnosis
Urinary sulfatide measurement to support diagnosis
Brain MRI to characterise white matter involvement
Nerve conduction studies and cerebrospinal fluid protein assessment
redFlags: Progressive loss of motor milestones in a previously well toddler
Combined central and peripheral neurological signs
Rapid cognitive or psychiatric deterioration in older patients
Feeding and swallowing difficulty with aspiration risk
reference.prognosis: The late-infantile form progresses rapidly to severe disability and death within a few years of onset. Juvenile and adult forms progress more slowly and variably. Presymptomatic or very early treatment with stem cell transplantation or gene therapy offers the best chance of altering the course, but symptomatic disease responds poorly.
pitfalls: Being misled by pseudodeficiency alleles that lower measured enzyme activity without causing disease
Attributing early behavioural or psychiatric changes in adults to a primary psychiatric disorder
Missing the peripheral neuropathy that helps distinguish it from other leukodystrophies
Delaying assessment for disease-modifying therapy until symptoms are advanced
management: Offer disease-modifying therapy to presymptomatic or very early patients: autologous ex-vivo ARSA gene-corrected haematopoietic stem cell gene therapy (atidarsagene autotemcel) or allogeneic haematopoietic stem cell transplantation in slower-progressing juvenile and adult forms
Manage spasticity with antispasticity agents such as baclofen supplemented by botulinum toxin, alongside physiotherapy and positioning
Control seizures with antiepileptic drugs and treat neuropathic pain and dystonia
Provide feeding support with gastrostomy, secretion management, and respiratory care as bulbar and motor function decline
Undertake surveillance with serial brain MRI, developmental and neurological review, and monitoring for gallbladder disease
Coordinate care through a metabolic, neurology, rehabilitation, and palliative care multidisciplinary team
Offer genetic counselling and test at-risk siblings for ARSA variants and enzyme deficiency, since presymptomatic identification enables curative early treatment
